title: Introducing AWS Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
content:
1. Background & The DevSecOps Triage Bottleneck In modern cloud-native development, AI-assisted coding tools have dramatically accelerated development velocity. However, this velocity also causes the volume of reported security vulnerabilities to scale exponentially.
Traditional static application security testing (SAST) and software composition analysis (SCA) tools typically generate thousands of raw findings daily, triggering severe operational fatigue. Conventional scanners inspect source code in isolation without understanding cloud infrastructure topology. As a result, a Critical severity finding on an internal offline developer utility receives the same alarm priority as a Medium flaw exposed on a public checkout API sitting directly in front of a payments database. Security teams expend days coordinating across application and infrastructure engineers just to answer a basic question: is this vulnerability truly reachable and exploitable in our live production environment? Crafting and shipping code patches often stalls because engineering teams lack the business context to safely evaluate the blast radius of proposed changes.
To resolve these chronic challenges, on October 22, 2026, AWS announced the General Availability (GA) of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities — an autonomous security service powered by frontier AI models that validates exploitable flaws and delivers remediations directly as reviewed pull requests in your repositories.
2. Architectural Breakthrough: How AWS Continuum Operates Unlike traditional alerting scanners, AWS Continuum establishes a closed-loop, automated remediation lifecycle connecting repository source code with live AWS infrastructure topology:
Continuum’s operational model is built on four core technological pillars:
Bidirectional Context Graph: Continuum correlates signals across repository source code and live AWS environments via the AWS Continuum Collector agent. The collector extracts telemetry from AWS Config, VPC routing, security groups, and IAM policies to determine whether vulnerable components are exposed to untrusted networks or handle sensitive data, prioritizing alerts based on actual business risk. Isolated Exploit Validation: For plausible vulnerabilities, Continuum spins up isolated managed sandboxes to execute reproducible proof-of-concept exploits. Findings receive explicit validation tiers (Static proven, Exploit verified), along with full attack path documentation and blast radius assessments. Automated Remediation Pull Requests: Once an exploit is verified, the AI Remediation Engine synthesizes a high-fidelity code fix (patching source logic, upgrading dependencies, or correcting resource policies). Continuum automatically opens a Pull Request named Continuum fix directly on GitHub/GitLab, complete with risk explanations and test evidence. Human-in-the-Loop Governance: Continuum never mutates source code or modifies production infrastructure autonomously. Every remediation is delivered as a standard pull request for engineer and tech lead review and approval prior to merging. 3. Hands-On Tour: AWS Console & GitHub Integration Within the AWS Management Console, the Continuum Overview dashboard provides centralized visibility across connected repositories, runtime environments, and collector health:
Instead of unprioritized alert backlogs, Continuum displays only issues proven to be exploitable, organized by operational severity and remediation readiness:
Each finding features a comprehensive risk report detailing validation proof (Static proven), reachability (Exploitable), potential tenant impact, and the exact lines of offending source code:
Most importantly, Continuum generates production-grade Pull Requests on GitHub with precise diffs and clear change rationales, enabling engineers to inspect, test, and merge remedies efficiently:
4. Key Takeaways for Cloud Engineers & DevSecOps Teams The release of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities represents a pivotal transition in cloud security:
From Passive Detection to Autonomous Remediation: Rather than merely routing defect tickets to developers, Continuum actively participates in the development lifecycle by authoring validated, production-ready code patches. Eliminating Dev-Sec Friction: Security teams receive verifiable proof of exploitability, while developers save hours of manual triage, sustaining feature velocity without compromising posture. Controlled Frontier AI Adoption: Continuum demonstrates how agentic AI can automate complex security engineering tasks while maintaining strict human approval boundaries. title: Event 1
content:
This event report documents the executive fireside chat held directly with Dr. Werner Vogels (Vice President & Chief Technology Officer at Amazon.com) and the AWS Community & Builders in Vietnam on October 02, 2026. It captures foundational architectural lessons on distributed systems at planetary scale, the historical genesis of Amazon DynamoDB, the operational resilience of GameDays, the philosophy of “The Renaissance Developer,” and the evolving role of software engineers in the Generative AI era.
Executive Summary: “The Renaissance Developer & Building for People” – In Conversation with Dr. Werner Vogels (CTO of Amazon) 📌 Event Overview Event Title: Fireside Chat with Dr. Werner Vogels: The Renaissance Developer & Building at Scale. Date & Time: 09:00 - 10:30, October 02, 2026. Location: 26th Floor, Bitexco Financial Tower, 02 Hai Trieu Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City. Keynote Speaker: Dr. Werner Vogels – Vice President & Chief Technology Officer (CTO) at Amazon.com. Moderator / Host: AWS Community Representatives, AWS Heroes & Community Builders Vietnam. Audience: AWS Community Builders, AWS Heroes, cloud architects, industry practitioners, and cloud intern engineers. Participant Role: Attendee / Intern Cloud Builder. Event Community Post: Facebook AWS Study Group 🎯 Key Event Objectives Direct Insights from the Chief Architect of Amazon & AWS: Uncovering firsthand, authentic engineering retrospectives detailing Amazon’s architectural transition from monolithic systems to decoupled, globally distributed infrastructure. Internalizing Amazon’s Product Philosophy: Deep-diving into the Working Backwards framework, rigorous tail-latency management at the 99.9th percentile (P99.9), and chaos engineering drills (GameDays). Defining “The Renaissance Developer”: Identifying the indispensable competencies that keep software engineers relevant, resilient, and empowered alongside rapid advancements in Generative AI. Bridging Global Cloud Leadership with Local Builder Culture: Celebrating the vibrant Vietnamese builder ecosystem (“A nation of builders, and a nation of coffee”), cultural connection through traditional drip coffee, and fostering professional pride among aspiring engineers. 💡 Core Takeaways Extracted from the Fireside Chat 1. The Genesis of Amazon DynamoDB: Lessons from a Catastrophic Holiday Outage The Historical Bottleneck: In the early 2000s, Amazon ran a promotional initiative offering free shipping on purchases exceeding $25 with delivery within two weeks. December 12 was the annual Christmas order cutoff date—the highest traffic shopping day of the entire year. Catastrophic Database Outage: A shared-disk commercial relational database cluster (RDBMS) storing core customer records encountered a severe concurrency bug under peak load, collapsing completely and remaining unavailable for an entire day. Amazon suffered millions of dollars in lost revenue. The Candid Retrospective: When vendor leadership convened with Werner, their initial response was: “You should have tested better!” While humbling, the vendor was right: Amazon was deploying commercial relational software far beyond its designed architectural boundaries. Groundbreaking Access-Pattern Research: Werner tasked Swami Sivasubramanian (then an Amazon intern, currently Vice President of AI at AWS) with auditing Amazon’s actual relational database usage patterns: 70% of access patterns: Were purely simple Key-Value operations (e.g., shopping cart retrieval requiring only a CustomerID; nobody was querying complex relational joins like “list all shopping carts containing a Harry Potter book”). 20% of workloads: Were single-table lookups requiring no relational joins. Only 10% of queries: Truly exercised relational schema capabilities. The Paradigm Shift: Using an expensive, monolithic relational engine for predominantly key-value workloads was an anti-pattern. Amazon committed to engineering its own purpose-built distributed storage engine, publishing the foundational Dynamo paper (2007), which paved the way for the fully managed Amazon DynamoDB service. 2. Operational Excellence & The Reality of Tail Latency (P99.9) The Median Latency Fallacy: Werner highlighted a common engineering blind spot: Measuring website responsiveness via median latency (e.g., 1.5 seconds) is fundamentally misleading. A median of 1.5 seconds means that 50% of your customers are experiencing worse performance! True operational excellence requires optimizing for the 99.9th Percentile (P99.9). Modern cloud architectures must be engineered to compress the entire tail latency distribution, guaranteeing that even the most impacted 0.1% of users experience responsive systems. GameDays and Chaos Engineering: Systems must be architected to withstand losing one or even two data centers (Availability Zones) simultaneously with zero customer disruption. Amazon instituted regular GameDays: Intentionally severing network connectivity or abruptly shutting down an entire data center without prior warning to test real-world failover automation. The Overlooked Challenge of Recovery & Reconciliation: While automated failover to remaining healthy data centers was quickly mastered, the team initially overlooked how to safely reconcile and bring the recovered data center back online with consistent state. Lesson: Architecting for failure requires not just surviving outages, but engineering complete, automated data reconciliation pipelines when disrupted infrastructure recovers. 3. Transforming Enterprise Cloud Economics Disrupting Long-Term Vendor Lock-in: Werner recalled that in his early years as CTO, vendor negotiations were fraught with predatory 5-to-10-year contracts requiring millions of dollars in upfront capital expenditure (CapEx) before technology was even deployed. The “Zero-Deposit Restaurant” Analogy: Werner analogized traditional IT procurement: Nobody walks into a restaurant in Vietnam and places 500,000 VND on the table before even knowing what food is served. AWS revolutionized IT by introducing true utility pricing: Pay-as-you-go—paying only for actual resource consumption with zero contractual obligations. Customers hold complete freedom to migrate away at any time, forcing cloud providers to continuously deliver operational value daily. S3’s Original Mission: When Amazon S3 launched in 2006, its tagline was simply “Storage for the Internet”—democratizing limitless scale for young web startups rather than catering solely to legacy corporate data centers. 4. The Profile of “The Renaissance Developer” Drawing from his landmark AWS re:Invent keynote, Werner elaborated on five vital qualities defining resilient engineering professionals:
Curiosity & Lifelong Learning: Tracing his own evolution from Pascal, COBOL, and Assembly to C, C++, Java, Python, and Rust, Werner stated that engineers must remain professional students throughout their careers. Quoting Rear Admiral Grace Hopper: “The most dangerous phrase in the language is, ‘We’ve always done it this way.’” Avoid locking your engineering identity into being just a “Java shop” or “Python shop.” System Thinking: Cultivate the ability to see the holistic architectural picture, understanding how discrete distributed services interact rather than narrowing focus to a single microservice or function. Communication – The Most Underrated Skill: Dispel the cinema stereotype of the isolated programmer coding in a dark basement. Engineers must excel at bridging customer problems and business objectives. When stakeholders demand “We need to use AI for this,” skilled engineers drill down to uncover the underlying challenge, evaluating whether complex models are truly required or if straightforward tools (like Amazon Rekognition) suffice. Uncompromising Ownership: Core tenet: “You own what you build.” Even when utilizing AI tools (Copilot, Claude, Cursor) to generate boilerplate code, any resulting bugs, performance regressions, or security vulnerabilities remain 100% your responsibility. Engineers cannot abdicate accountability to an AI tool. Polymath / T-Shaped Breadth: Cultivate deep specialization in a primary domain (e.g., distributed databases) while maintaining sufficient breadth across UI, networking, and business logic to collaborate seamlessly across cross-functional teams. 5. Artificial Intelligence: An Amplifier for Human Ingenuity AI in Perspective: Artificial Intelligence is not a novel phenomenon of the last two years; the discipline originated in 1956 with John McCarthy and Marvin Minsky. As McCarthy famously remarked: “As soon as it works, we don’t call it AI anymore”—it becomes standard search, computer vision, or forecasting algorithms. AI as a Next-Generation Compiler: Traditional compilers take precise, structured programming language code and emit machine code that humans do not need to inspect. Generative AI operates inversely: It receives imprecise natural language prompts and generates structured source code. Because natural language is inherently ambiguous, AI cannot say “I don’t know” and will hallucinate. Therefore, human code reviews and rigorous automated verification are non-negotiable. Amazon’s “Working Backwards” Framework: Long before writing implementation code, teams author a mock Press Release and Customer FAQs (PR/FAQ). Generative AI accelerates early-stage prototyping, compressing weeks of proof-of-concept development into hours. Human-Centric Technology Philosophy: “We build technology for people, not for technology’s sake.”
Technology is ultimately a tool. Enduring engineering value stems from uniquely human traits: Sound Judgment, Empathy, Intuitive Insight, and Professional Pride. 🎁 Cultural Highlight: Connecting with the Vietnam Builder Community Representatives from the AWS Vietnam Community presented Dr. Werner Vogels with a traditional Vietnamese Phin Coffee Filter set paired with premium local coffee beans. Werner enthusiastically shared his appreciation for “Cà phê sữa đá” (Vietnamese iced milk coffee) and praised the energy, humility, and technical ambition of Vietnam’s growing builder community. Closing message: Take pride in community contributions and empower peers so that the entire tech ecosystem scales collectively. 🚀 Direct Application to Cloud Internship & Engineering Practice Incorporating P99.9 Tail Latency Benchmarks: Evaluate deployed architectures beyond simple functional checks by simulating heavy load, tracking percentile metrics via CloudWatch, and calibrating Auto Scaling policies. Practicing Multi-AZ Resilience & Disaster Recovery: Rigorously configure Multi-AZ failover for Amazon RDS and Amazon ElastiCache, while designing explicit data reconciliation procedures for post-incident recovery. Rigorous Accountability with AI-Generated Code: Leverage generative developer tools to amplify productivity while rigorously auditing every generated line of infrastructure-as-code and application logic. Honing Technical Communication: Craft architectural documentation, worklogs, and presentation narratives that are articulate and actionable for both technical and business stakeholders. 📸 Event Photo Highlights & Attendance Proof Below are on-site photographs captured during the Fireside Chat with Dr. Werner Vogels on the 26th Floor of the Bitexco Financial Tower:
1. Dr. Werner Vogels on the Fireside Chat Stage Figure 1: Dr. Werner Vogels (VP & CTO of Amazon.com) in conversation with Nguyen Gia Hung (Solutions Architect Manager) and My Nguyen (Sr Prototyping Architect, AWS Vietnam) at the 26th Floor, Bitexco.
2. Community Group Photo with Dr. Werner Vogels Figure 2: Memorable group photo bringing together AWS Heroes, AWS Community Builders, and First Cloud Journey intern engineers alongside Dr. Werner Vogels.
3. Intern Engineering Cohort at the Event Figure 3: First Cloud Journey intern team checking in at the AWS office (26th floor Bitexco) in front of the Amazon Leadership Principle wall “Invent and Simplify”.
Retrospective: Interacting with Dr. Werner Vogels provided invaluable architectural wisdom and deep inspiration, reinforcing the mindset of continuous learning, rigorous engineering ownership, and human-centric cloud innovation.

content:
Week 1 Objectives: Familiarize with cloud computing fundamentals and foundational infrastructure services following the Explore AWS Services curriculum on The First Cloud Journey. Master initial cost governance principles using AWS Budgets and implement robust identity governance according to the principle of least privilege with AWS IAM. Hands-on architecting and provisioning of isolated cloud networks (Amazon VPC), compute instance management (Amazon EC2), and object storage hosting (Amazon S3). Dedicate Friday to synthesizing weekly technical knowledge, finalizing comprehensive Worklog documentation, and formulating initial concepts for the internship Capstone Project Proposal. Tasks to be Carried Out This Week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material Monday Cost Governance & Identity Security: - Establishing account governance & budget alerts with AWS Budgets (000007). - Identity management and access control with AWS IAM (000002). - Enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all administrative access paths. 09/14/2026 09/14/2026 000007 & 000002 Tuesday Core Networking Infrastructure (VPC Essentials): - Provisioning an isolated cloud network via Amazon VPC (000003) (Subnets, Route Tables, Internet Gateway). - Implementing structural segregation between Public Subnets (Internet-facing) and Private Subnets (DB/Backend). 09/15/2026 09/15/2026 Amazon VPC Workshop (000003) Wednesday Elastic Compute Services (EC2 Compute Basics): - Launching and configuring virtual servers with Amazon EC2 (000004). - Configuring Security Groups, Key Pairs, SSH terminal connectivity, and web server installation. 09/16/2026 09/16/2026 Amazon EC2 Workshop (000004) Thursday Object Storage & Static Website Hosting (S3 Storage): - Provisioning S3 Buckets, uploading objects, and managing Storage Classes with Amazon S3 (000057). - Enabling Static Website Hosting and configuring public-read Bucket Policies. 09/17/2026 09/17/2026 Amazon S3 Workshop (000057) Friday Week 1 Review, Worklog Completion & Project Work: - Knowledge Review: Consolidate foundational services mastered throughout the week (IAM, VPC, EC2, S3). - Worklog Completion: Finalize bilingual Week 1 documentation and execute clean resource teardowns. - Project Work: Analyze business constraints and technical requirements for the Capstone Project Proposal. 09/18/2026 09/18/2026 FCAJ Roadmap Daily In-Depth Learning Outcomes & Key Takeaways: 📌 Monday (09/14/2026) - Cost Governance (AWS Budgets) & Identity Security (AWS IAM) What did we learn today? Proactive Cloud FinOps via AWS Budgets: Mitigated “bill shock” risks by establishing automated financial guardrails before deploying cloud infrastructure. Configured a Monthly Cost Budget capped at $10.00. Configured two automated notification thresholds: Actual spend reaching 80% ($8.00) and Forecasted spend reaching 100% ($10.00), triggering instant alert emails to prevent budget overruns. Zero-Trust Identity Hardening via AWS IAM: Locked down the Root Account, strictly adhering to the principle of never utilizing root credentials for day-to-day engineering activities. Created a dedicated IAM User admin-dev for hands-on technical operations. Enforced role-based access through IAM User Groups rather than attaching direct user policies, associating the AdministratorAccess AWS Managed Policy according to the principle of least privilege. Enforced strict Password Policies: minimum 12 characters requiring uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Enforced Virtual Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) via Google Authenticator across both Root and IAM User accounts. Figure 1.1.1: IAM identity governance topology enforcing least privilege resource access control.
Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Budget Notification Email Not Delivering: Email address syntax typo during budget creation prevented delivery. Solution: Verified notification parameters within AWS Budgets, resubmitted the recipient address, and confirmed the SNS subscription confirmation link via Gmail. MFA Lockout Risk During Device Reset: Acknowledged the critical best practice of securely archiving the MFA backup seed key offline to mitigate permanent account lockout. 📌 Tuesday (09/15/2026) - Isolated Cloud Networking via Amazon VPC What did we learn today? Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Subnet Topologies: Defined Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) blocks, creating VPC fcaj-vpc with 10.0.0.0/16 (allocating 65,536 private IP addresses). Subdivided the network across two Availability Zones (us-east-1a and us-east-1b): Public Subnets: 10.0.1.0/24 (AZ-a) and 10.0.2.0/24 (AZ-b) allocated for edge workloads (ALB, Web Servers). Enabled Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address. Private Subnets: 10.0.10.0/24 (AZ-a) and 10.0.20.0/24 (AZ-b) reserved for databases and application tiers, completely isolated from direct internet access. Traffic Routing via Internet Gateway & Route Tables: Provisioned Internet Gateway fcaj-igw and attached it to VPC fcaj-vpc. Created Public-Route-Table, added a default route 0.0.0.0/0 targeting fcaj-igw, and associated both Public Subnets. Created Private-Route-Table containing solely local internal routing 10.0.0.0/16 local, ensuring total internet isolation for backend workloads. Figure 1.1.2: Amazon VPC resource topology with multi-AZ subnets and active Internet Gateway routing.
Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Public Subnet Instances Lacking Public IPs: Launched instances only acquired private addresses. Root cause: Newly provisioned custom subnets do not enable auto-assigning public IPv4 addresses by default. Solution: Selected Public Subnet ➔ Actions ➔ Edit subnet settings ➔ Enabled Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address. 📌 Wednesday (09/16/2026) - Elastic Compute Operations with Amazon EC2 What did we learn today? EC2 Virtual Machine Lifecycle & Configuration: Deployed the Amazon Linux 2023 AMI optimized for AWS Nitro system architectures. Selected the t2.micro instance tier (1 vCPU, 1GB RAM) under AWS Free Tier eligibility. Generated an RSA cryptographic key pair fcaj-keypair.pem for secure remote terminal access. Virtual Firewall Hardening via Security Groups: Provisioned web-server-sg bound to fcaj-vpc. Inbound rule configuration: Port 22 (SSH): Strictly restricted to My IP to prevent automated brute-force attempts from public internet scanners. Port 80 (HTTP): Open to 0.0.0.0/0 to allow worldwide web traffic. SSH Terminal Execution & Web Daemon Provisioning: chmod 400 fcaj-keypair.pem ssh -i "fcaj-keypair.pem" ec2-user@<EC2-PUBLIC-IP> sudo dnf update -y sudo dnf install -y httpd sudo systemctl start httpd sudo systemctl enable httpd echo "<h1>Welcome to AWS First Cloud Journey - EC2 Running!</h1>" | sudo tee /var/www/html/index.html Figure 1.1.3: Amazon EC2 compute instance operating in running state on AWS.
Encountered Challenges & Solutions: SSH Key Permission Error (Permissions 0644 are too open): SSH rejected connection attempts. Root cause: Overly permissive key file access permissions. Solution: Executed chmod 400 fcaj-keypair.pem on Unix terminals (or stripped inherited permissions via Windows security settings). 📌 Thursday (09/17/2026) - Object Storage & Static Website Hosting via Amazon S3 What did we learn today? Cloud Object Storage Fundamentals with Amazon S3: Mastered the Global Namespace requirement: Bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS regions and adhere to DNS naming conventions. Created bucket fcaj-static-web-887086382708. Analyzed cost-optimization storage classes: S3 Standard (frequent access), S3 Standard-IA (infrequent access with millisecond retrieval), and S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval (long-term archival). Enabled Bucket Versioning to safeguard assets against accidental overwrites and deletions. Static Website Hosting Deployment: Enabled Static website hosting, designating index.html as the index document and error.html as the error document. Disabled Block Public Access (BPA) strictly for this public-facing web hosting bucket. Applied a public-read Bucket Policy granting anonymous GET permissions: { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "PublicReadGetObject", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": "*", "Action": "s3:GetObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::fcaj-static-web-887086382708/*" } ] } Successfully verified website availability via the S3 website endpoint: http://fcaj-static-web-887086382708.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: HTTP 403 Forbidden on S3 Website Endpoint: Browser returned access denied. Root cause: Missing public-read bucket policy or failure to uncheck all four Block Public Access toggles. Solution: Updated the bucket policy JSON and confirmed the public access toggle release. 📌 Friday (09/18/2026) - Week 1 Review, Worklog Finalization & Proposal Research What did we learn today? Core Infrastructure Architecture Synthesis: Identity (IAM): Outer perimeter gatekeeper defining Who can do What. Network (VPC): Isolation boundary and traffic routing backbone. Compute (EC2): Workload processing engine hosting scalable application daemons. Storage (S3): Durable object repository delivering 99.999999999% (11 9s) of data durability. FinOps Resource Hygiene: Stopped EC2 instances when idle to conserve Free Tier runtime hours (750 hours/month), and released unattached Elastic IPs to avoid idle reservation fees. Capstone Project Proposal Formulation: Synthesized architectural concepts toward building a resilient Two-Tier Web Application integrating Auto Scaling and managed relational databases on AWS.

title: Introduction
content:
VPC endpoints VPC endpoints are virtual devices. They are horizontally scaled, redundant, and highly available VPC components. They allow communication between your compute resources and AWS services without imposing availability risks. Compute resources running in VPC can access Amazon S3 using a Gateway endpoint. PrivateLink interface endpoints can be used by compute resources running in VPC or on-premises. Workshop overview In this workshop, you will use two VPCs.
“VPC Cloud” is for cloud resources such as a Gateway endpoint and an EC2 instance to test with. “VPC On-Prem” simulates an on-premises environment such as a factory or corporate datacenter. An EC2 instance running strongSwan VPN software has been deployed in “VPC On-prem” and automatically configured to establish a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel with AWS Transit Gateway. This VPN simulates connectivity from an on-premises location to the AWS cloud. To minimize costs, only one VPN instance is provisioned to support this workshop. When planning VPN connectivity for your production workloads, AWS recommends using multiple VPN devices for high availability.

Harvest Report: “First Cloud AI Journey” Meetup (October 24, 2026) 📌 Event Overview Event Name: First Cloud AI Journey Meetup: Trends & Real-world Practices in Cloud & AI Agent Deployment Date & Time: 09:00 – 12:00, Saturday Morning, October 24, 2026 Location: AWS Vietnam Office, 26th Floor, Bitexco Financial Tower, 02 Hai Trieu Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City Organizers: First Cloud Journey (FCJ) in collaboration with AWS Community Builders and AWS Student Builder Groups Role: Attendee & First Cloud Journey Intern Audience: Over 100 technology engineers, including Tech Leads, Cloud Solutions Architects, DevOps/Security Engineers from enterprises, AWS Community Builders, alongside passionate students and interns eager to master Cloud Computing and Generative AI Agents. Event Community Post: Facebook AWS Study Group 🎯 Objectives & Expectations Explore Production-grade AI Agent Architectures: Gain deep insights into how industry practitioners combine core AWS cloud infrastructure with modern Generative AI to deploy autonomous agents in production environments. Learn Enterprise-level Technical Solutions: Grasp real-world challenges and concrete technical remedies: optimizing latency for Vietnamese Voice AI, centralized multi-account networking with AWS RAM, automated shift-left security testing with AI Pentesting agents, and context window/memory management. Expand Professional Community Networking: Directly connect and engage with Tech Leads, AWS Community Builders, and senior enterprise engineers to glean career advice and cultivate a mature engineering mindset. 🎤 In-Depth Technical Sessions Breakdown The meetup delivered condensed, highly actionable technical insights through five curated sessions:
1. Session 1: Hear, Think, Speak - Building a Vietnamese Voice-AI Contact Center on AWS Mr. Kiet Tran (Founder & AI Engineer at Revve AI) detailing the architectural nuances between Cascade, Speech-to-Speech (S2S), and Full-duplex S2S voice systems.
Speaker: Mr. Kiet Tran – Founder & AI Engineer at Revve AI. Core Technical Insights: Three Architectural Paradigms for Voice Agents: Cascade Pipeline: Serial chaining of ASR (Speech-to-Text) ➔ LLM (Text-to-Text) ➔ TTS (Text-to-Speech). Key advantage: an explicit text checkpoint in the middle enabling strict guardrail enforcement and auditability. Speech-to-Speech (S2S): A unified speech model (e.g., Amazon Nova 2 Sonic) ingesting raw audio and outputting direct speech. Operates in half-duplex mode: user barge-in immediately interrupts and halts bot audio playback. Full-duplex S2S: Continuous bidirectional audio streaming (e.g., OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live), empowering the bot to respond naturally with backchannel interjections (“yes”, “uh-huh”) and seamless vocal overlap just like human conversation. Four Practical Lessons Paid in Production: Vietnamese Tone & Turn Detection Accuracy (79% vs 94%): Vietnamese acoustic intonation and tone diacritics cause high false cut-off rates under English-centric algorithms ➔ Mandatory requirement to benchmark directly on native Vietnamese audio datasets. Raw Number Pronunciation Quirks (“500K” read as abbreviation instead of “five hundred thousand”): Untreated text fed to TTS engines leads to mispronunciations ➔ Requires a dedicated Text Normalization layer prior to speech synthesis. Sentence-level Guardrails (Guard per Sentence): Streaming output without fine-grained checkpoints risks playing inappropriate opening words to callers (5 out of 6 leak cases). Enforcing an intermediate Small Judge Model to evaluate each sentence before TTS reduced violations to 0 out of 6. Latency Budget Management: Strict constraint to cap total round-trip latency under ~1.8s for smooth conversational flow, mandating a median LLM latency budget between 0.24s and 1.15s (e.g., self-hosted Gemma models). Live Demo: Live automated phone call interview screening a candidate for a Cloud Engineer position in natural Vietnamese, demonstrating fluid turn-taking, prompt understanding, and context-aware responses. 2. Session 2: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) - Create Once, Share Everywhere Mr. Long Huynh (Solutions Engineer at Styl Solution) addressing multi-account infrastructure fragmentation and demonstrating how AWS RAM enables centralized, cost-effective resource sharing.
Speaker: Mr. Long Huynh – Solutions Engineer at Styl Solution. Core Technical Insights: The Multi-Account Challenge: In enterprise environments spanning multiple AWS accounts (for different departments, business units, or SDLC stages like Dev, Staging, and Production), duplicating shared network infrastructure (Transit Gateways, VPC Subnets, Route 53 Resolver Rules, License Manager) incurs 3x cost inflation, configuration drift, and decentralized governance. The AWS RAM Paradigm: Implements the core principle: “Create once, share securely across the entire organization (AWS Organizations)”. Infrastructure is provisioned once within an authoritative Owner Account and shared seamlessly via Resource Shares to Member Accounts. Consumer Accounts consume these shared assets natively within their own AWS Console interfaces without administrative overhead. Dual-layer Governance (IAM Policies combined with SCPs): Combines granular IAM Resource-based Policies with organization-wide Service Control Policies (SCPs) to establish immutable permission guardrails, preventing member accounts from altering or bypassing shared network topologies. 3. Session 3: AWS Pentest with AWS Continuum / Security Agent Mr. Nguyen Tuan Thinh (Security Engineer at Styl Solution) engaging with audience inquiries regarding autonomous security agents and automated CI/CD pentesting on SIT/UAT.
Speaker: Mr. Nguyen Tuan Thinh – Security Engineer at Styl Solution. Core Technical Insights: The Shift-Left Security Philosophy: Embedding security verification into the earliest phases of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) rather than treating it as an afterthought before release. Automated Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Auditing: Integrating automated security bots into GitHub and GitLab Pull Request (PR) pipelines. Performing Static Code Analysis on Terraform scripts to detect vulnerabilities such as unrestricted 0.0.0.0/0 ingress rules, unencrypted EBS volumes/S3 buckets, or overprivileged wildcard IAM policies (*) before code is merged. Frontier Security Agent: Powered by Amazon Bedrock foundation models with autonomous reasoning capabilities to plan and execute comprehensive security evaluations without human intervention. Acts as an active simulated adversary (Attacker) performing penetration testing against SIT and UAT staging environments to uncover business logic flaws and configuration oversights before production deployment. 4. Session 4: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore - Production Architecture & Dual Memory System Mr. Xuan An (Leader of AWS Student Builder Group HCMUTE) explaining single-session ephemeral MicroVMs on EC2 Spot instances for cost-optimized agent runtimes.
Speaker: Mr. Xuan An – Leader of AWS Student Builder Group HCMUTE. Core Technical Insights: Agent Ecosystem Architecture: A modular framework harmonizing Application Layer ➔ Agent Runtime (framework, instructions, local tools, context) ➔ Foundation Models. Cost-effective Agent Runtime on EC2 Spot Instances: Instead of maintaining expensive, long-running servers, the runtime orchestrates lightweight MicroVMs dynamically provisioned on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Ephemeral Context Principle: “Micro lives to serve a single session only” – Each MicroVM encapsulates session data (Disk and Memory) exclusively for the duration of one user dialogue. Upon session completion, the instance is promptly recycled, slashing operational compute expenses by 70% to 90%. Dual-tier Memory System: Short-term Memory: Synchronous in-session state retention to maintain immediate conversational context. Long-term Memory: Asynchronous post-session extraction of user preferences, core facts, and critical historical decisions into Vector Databases (OpenSearch / Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases) to ensure persistent personalization across subsequent interactions. 5. Session 5: Kiro Crew - All-In-One AI Companion for Engineers Mr. Danh Hoang Hieu Nghi (AWS Community Builder) and Mr. Kieu Nguyen Dang Khoa (Tech Lead ACB) demonstrating live developer storage inspection and token breakdown.
Speakers: Mr. Kieu Nguyen Dang Khoa (Technical Lead – Digital Transformation at ACB Bank) & Mr. Danh Hoang Hieu Nghi (AWS Community Builder). Core Technical Insights & Live Demonstrations: 24/7 Engineer Companion: Platform architecture designed to continuously assist software engineers with code reviews, architectural compliance checks, and infrastructure health monitoring. Automated Visual UI Artifacts Generation: Demonstrating an end-to-end workflow where the agent autonomously crawls real-world tech job market listings, synthesizes key data points, and renders interactive UI chart artifacts directly inside the chat interface. Context Window Management Strategies: Auto Compact Mechanism: Automatically triggered when conversation context reaches 70% – 90% of model token limits, intelligently summarizing earlier dialogue turns to liberate token capacity without dropping conversational coherence. Context Breakdown Inspector: Enables engineers to dissect token consumption across System Prompts, Tool/Function Schemas, Memory, and User Messages, facilitating cost and performance tuning. Developer Storage Management & Security Guardrails: Selective memory cleanup algorithms targeting stale or unneeded storage keys to avoid database bloat. Robust Guardrails: Enforcing strict execution policies that prohibit destructive commands (such as terminating core instances or dropping database schemas) and sanitize model responses to prevent secret/credential leakage (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, API tokens). 💡 Key Takeaways & Lessons Learned FinOps & Latency Budget Trade-offs: In Voice AI and real-time agent workflows, every millisecond counts. Model selection (Cascade vs S2S, Cloud APIs vs Self-hosted Open Source) must be strictly governed by latency thresholds and cost-efficiency rather than chasing parameter size blindly. Centralized Multi-Account Governance with AWS RAM: Enterprise architectures demand centralized resource ownership combined with seamless distributed consumption. Combining AWS RAM with SCPs provides a battle-tested blueprint for scalable multi-account organizations. Empowering Security via Autonomous Shift-Left Agents: Security testing is evolving from manual periodic audits into automated, agentic CI/CD verifications, identifying infrastructure vulnerabilities before code reaches production environments. Mastering Agent Context and Memory Hygiene: Implementing dynamic context compaction (Auto Compact) alongside dual-tier memory structures (Short-term vs Long-term) is crucial for delivering highly capable, cost-efficient, and reliable AI systems. 🚀 Practical Application to FCJ Internship & Cloud Projects Implement Safety Guardrails in Automated Scripts: Always incorporate pre-flight validation checks and safety boundaries into automated infrastructure scripts to prevent unintended modifications or deletions. Event-Driven Serverless Compute with AWS Lambda: Mastered serverless compute abstraction: Eliminating OS patching and capacity management, executing code only in response to discrete triggers. Developed an automated maintenance function ec2-nightly-stop in Python using Boto3 to discover development instances matching Environment = Development and issue termination signals at 20:00 daily. Streamed execution telemetry into CloudWatch Logs Group /aws/lambda/ec2-nightly-stop, measuring cold-start durations of 1.2 seconds and memory allocations under 64MB. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: AccessDeniedException on Function Execution: The Lambda handler failed with unauthorized API call errors when invoking EC2 APIs. Root cause: Default basic execution roles only permit writing CloudWatch Logs. Solution: Created an IAM customer-managed policy authorizing ec2:DescribeInstances and ec2:StopInstances attached to the function execution role. 📌 Tuesday (09/22/2026) - Security Hardening & Cryptographic Key Management What did we learn today? Envelope Encryption & Lifecycle Governance with AWS KMS: Differentiated between AWS Managed Keys and Customer Managed Keys (CMK). Created symmetric CMK fcaj-data-encryption-key, defining granular Key Policies controlling which IAM principals can invoke kms:Encrypt and kms:Decrypt. Enabled Automatic Annual Key Rotation without changing key ARNs. Applied CMK encryption across Amazon EBS storage volumes and Amazon S3 objects (SSE-KMS) with full audit logging in CloudTrail. Web Application Defense via AWS WAF: Created and deployed a regional Web ACL protecting Application Load Balancers. Configured pre-packaged AWS Managed Rules: Core rule set (CRS) for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, Amazon IP reputation list blocking malicious scanners, and a Rate-based rule capping traffic at 100 requests per 5 minutes per IP. Intelligent Threat Detection with Amazon GuardDuty: Activated GuardDuty to passively analyze VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail management events using machine learning to detect port scans and compromised credentials. Figure 1.2.2: S3 data-at-rest encryption control model governed by AWS KMS and audited via CloudTrail.
Figure 1.2.3: Perimeter defense shield protecting application entry points against web threats using AWS WAF.
Encountered Challenges & Solutions: False-Positive Block on Legitimate API Payloads: Valid client requests were blocked with HTTP 403 by the GenericRFI_BODY rule. Solution: Inspected CloudWatch WAF metrics to identify the specific rule ID, toggled the rule to Count mode to log telemetry without dropping packets, and configured path-specific rule exclusions. 📌 Wednesday (09/23/2026) - Resilience & Serverless Microservices Containers What did we learn today? Serverless Container Orchestration with Amazon ECS Fargate: Packaged microservice application code into Docker images and published versioned artifacts to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR). Authored ECS Task Definitions specifying container compute footprints (0.25 vCPU, 512MB RAM), eliminating underlying host OS administration. Launched an ECS Service running on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer with dynamic health checking and self-healing task replacement. Continuous Delivery Automation via AWS CodePipeline: Engineered an automated CI/CD pipeline: Pulling source updates from GitHub ➔ Triggering AWS CodeBuild to compile Docker images and execute unit tests ➔ Executing rolling deployments to ECS Fargate tasks with zero downtime. Figure 1.2.5: Successful automated build and deployment report in AWS CodeBuild.
Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Docker Hub Pull Rate Limiting in CodeBuild: Builds failed during base image acquisition. Solution: Updated Dockerfiles to pull official base images from the Amazon ECR Public Gallery (public.ecr.aws/docker/library/), bypassing third-party rate limits and improving download speeds over AWS internal networks. 📌 Thursday (09/24/2026) - Cost Optimization & Telemetry Analytics What did we learn today? Strategic Cloud Financial Management: Analyzed cost structures across On-Demand, Spot instances (up to 90% discount for fault-tolerant workloads), and 1- to 3-year commitments (Savings Plans & Reserved Instances). For steady-state 24/7 database and backend tiers, Compute Savings Plans yield 45% to 66% sustained cost reductions compared to standard On-Demand pricing. Serverless Telemetry Analytics with AWS Glue & Athena: Configured AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) delivering granular hourly billing manifests into an S3 bucket. Deployed an AWS Glue Crawler to discover report schemas and generate partition metadata in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Executed serverless SQL queries in Amazon Athena to identify spending spikes per service, peak regional usage hours, and unattached idle EBS volumes. Figure 1.2.6: Cloud cost data extraction, cataloging, and analytical query workflow utilizing AWS Glue and Amazon Athena.
Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Athena Syntax Errors Reading Compressed CUR Manifests: Direct queries threw syntax errors on gzipped micro-batch files. Solution: Deployed the automated CloudFormation integration template provided by AWS CUR, configuring standardized month-based partition indexing for Athena. 📌 Friday (09/25/2026) - Week 2 Review, Worklog Finalization & Proposal Formulation What did we learn today? AWS Well-Architected Pillar Synthesis: Operational Excellence: Event-driven automation with Lambda and observability via CloudWatch. Security: Envelope encryption via KMS and perimeter defense via WAF. Reliability: Microservices containerization via ECS Fargate and automated CI/CD deployments. Cost Optimization: Strategic commitment models and serverless billing audits with Athena. In this section, we configure the Amazon Cognito User Pool (exammaker-dev-users) on the Essentials tier (free up to ≤ 10,000 MAU), register a browser-based Single-page application (SPA) client (exammaker-dev-spa) using OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE, and create 3 RBAC role groups (admin, head, teacher).
1. Create User Pool & SPA Application Step 1: Create the User Pool and SPA App Client Open Amazon Cognito in ap-southeast-1 → select User pools → click Create user pool. Configure the initial application details: Application type: Single-page application (SPA) (Public client without a browser-exposed Client Secret). Name your application (App client): exammaker-dev-spa. User pool name: exammaker-dev-users (ESSENTIALS tier — Free Tier ≤ 10,000 MAU). Options for sign-in identifiers: select Email (case-insensitive). Step 2: Disable Self-registration & Configure Return URL Under Configure options: Self-registration: Unchecked / Disabled (AllowAdminCreateUserOnly = true) — only school administrators can provision teacher accounts, preventing unauthorized public sign-ups from abusing Amazon Bedrock quotas. Required attributes for sign-up: select email. Return URL: enter http://localhost:3000/auth/callback/ (matching Next.js trailingSlash: true). Click Create user directory to complete creation. 2. Configure Managed Login, PKCE & Scopes Step 1: Configure Callback & Sign-out URLs Navigate to App clients → exammaker-dev-spa → Login pages tab → Edit. Add the allowed URLs for both local development (localhost) and production (app.khaothiai.xyz): Allowed callback URLs: http://localhost:3000/auth/callback/ https://app.khaothiai.xyz/auth/callback/ Allowed sign-out URLs: http://localhost:3000/ https://app.khaothiai.xyz/ Identity providers: Cognito user pool. Step 2: Configure OAuth 2.0 Grant Types, Scopes & Token TTL OAuth 2.0 grant types: Enable Authorization code grant only (with PKCE; keep legacy Implicit grant disabled). OpenID Connect scopes (3 scopes): select Email, OpenID, and Profile. Token Expiration (TTL): Access Token: 60 minutes ID Token: 60 minutes Refresh Token: 7 days Click Save changes. 3. content:
⚠️ Note: The information below is for reference purposes only. Please do not copy verbatim for your report, including this warning.
In this section, you need to summarize the contents of the workshop that you plan to conduct.
IoT Weather Platform for Lab Research A Unified AWS Serverless Solution for Real-Time Weather Monitoring 1. Executive Summary The IoT Weather Platform is designed for the ITea Lab team in Ho Chi Minh City to enhance weather data collection and analysis. It supports up to 5 weather stations, with potential scalability to 10-15, utilizing Raspberry Pi edge devices with ESP32 sensors to transmit data via MQTT. The platform leverages AWS Serverless services to deliver real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and cost efficiency, with access restricted to 5 lab members via Amazon Cognito.
2. Problem Statement What’s the Problem? Current weather stations require manual data collection, becoming unmanageable with multiple units. There is no centralized system for real-time data or analytics, and third-party platforms are costly and overly complex.
The Solution The platform uses AWS IoT Core to ingest MQTT data, AWS Lambda and API Gateway for processing, Amazon S3 for storage (including a data lake), and AWS Glue Crawlers and ETL jobs to extract, transform, and load data from the S3 data lake to another S3 bucket for analysis. AWS Amplify with Next.js provides the web interface, and Amazon Cognito ensures secure access. Similar to Thingsboard and CoreIoT, users can register new devices and manage connections, though this platform operates on a smaller scale and is designed for private use. Key features include real-time dashboards, trend analysis, and low operational costs.
Benefits and Return on Investment The solution establishes a foundational resource for lab members to develop a larger IoT platform, serving as a study resource, and provides a data foundation for AI enthusiasts for model training or analysis. It reduces manual reporting for each station via a centralized platform, simplifying management and maintenance, and improves data reliability. Monthly costs are $0.66 USD per the AWS Pricing Calculator, with a 12-month total of $7.92 USD. All IoT equipment costs are covered by the existing weather station setup, eliminating additional development expenses. The break-even period of 6-12 months is achieved through significant time savings from reduced manual work.
3. Solution Architecture The platform employs a serverless AWS architecture to manage data from 5 Raspberry Pi-based stations, scalable to 15. Data is ingested via AWS IoT Core, stored in an S3 data lake, and processed by AWS Glue Crawlers and ETL jobs to transform and load it into another S3 bucket for analysis. Lambda and API Gateway handle additional processing, while Amplify with Next.js hosts the dashboard, secured by Cognito. The architecture is detailed below:
AWS Services Used AWS IoT Core: Ingests MQTT data from 5 stations, scalable to 15. AWS Lambda: Processes data and triggers Glue jobs (two functions). Amazon API Gateway: Facilitates web app communication. Amazon S3: Stores raw data in a data lake and processed outputs (two buckets). AWS Glue: Crawlers catalog data, and ETL jobs transform and load it. AWS Amplify: Hosts the Next.js web interface. Amazon Cognito: Secures access for lab users. Component Design Edge Devices: Raspberry Pi collects and filters sensor data, sending it to IoT Core. Data Ingestion: AWS IoT Core receives MQTT messages from the edge devices. Data Storage: Raw data is stored in an S3 data lake; processed data is stored in another S3 bucket. Data Processing: AWS Glue Crawlers catalog the data, and ETL jobs transform it for analysis. Web Interface: AWS Amplify hosts a Next.js app for real-time dashboards and analytics. User Management: Amazon Cognito manages user access, allowing up to 5 active accounts. 4. Technical Implementation Implementation Phases This project has two parts—setting up weather edge stations and building the weather platform—each following 4 phases:
Build Theory and Draw Architecture: Research Raspberry Pi setup with ESP32 sensors and design the AWS serverless architecture (1 month pre-internship) Calculate Price and Check Practicality: Use AWS Pricing Calculator to estimate costs and adjust if needed (Month 1). Fix Architecture for Cost or Solution Fit: Tweak the design (e.g., optimize Lambda with Next.js) to stay cost-effective and usable (Month 2). Develop, Test, and Deploy: Code the Raspberry Pi setup, AWS services with CDK/SDK, and Next.js app, then test and release to production (Months 2-3). Technical Requirements
Weather Edge Station: Sensors (temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed), a microcontroller (ESP32), and a Raspberry Pi as the edge device. Raspberry Pi runs Raspbian, handles Docker for filtering, and sends 1 MB/day per station via MQTT over Wi-Fi. Weather Platform: Practical knowledge of AWS Amplify (hosting Next.js), Lambda (minimal use due to Next.js), AWS Glue (ETL), S3 (two buckets), IoT Core (gateway and rules), and Cognito (5 users). Use AWS CDK/SDK to code interactions (e.g., IoT Core rules to S3). Next.js reduces Lambda workload for the fullstack web app. 5. Timeline & Milestones Project Timeline
Pre-Internship (Month 0): 1 month for planning and old station review. Internship (Months 1-3): 3 months. Month 1: Study AWS and upgrade hardware. Month 2: Design and adjust architecture. Month 3: Implement, test, and launch. Post-Launch: Up to 1 year for research. 6. Budget Estimation You can find the detailed budget estimation directly on the AWS Pricing Calculator.
Infrastructure Costs AWS Services: AWS Lambda: $0.00/month (1,000 requests, 512 MB storage). S3 Standard: $0.15/month (6 GB, 2,100 requests, 1 GB scanned). Data Transfer: $0.02/month (1 GB inbound, 1 GB outbound). AWS Amplify: $0.35/month (256 MB, 500 ms requests). Amazon API Gateway: $0.01/month (2,000 requests). AWS Glue ETL Jobs: $0.02/month (2 DPUs). AWS Glue Crawlers: $0.07/month (1 crawler). MQTT (IoT Core): $0.08/month (5 devices, 45,000 messages). Total: $0.7/month, $8.40/12 months
Hardware: $265 one-time (Raspberry Pi 5 and sensors). 7. Risk Assessment Risk Matrix Network Outages: Medium impact, medium probability. Sensor Failures: High impact, low probability. Cost Overruns: Medium impact, low probability. Mitigation Strategies Network: Local storage on Raspberry Pi with Docker. Sensors: Regular checks and spares. Cost: AWS budget alerts and optimization. Contingency Plans Revert to manual methods if AWS fails. Use CloudFormation for cost-related rollbacks. 8. Expected Outcomes Technical Improvements: Real-time data and analytics replace manual processes.
Scalable to 10-15 stations.
Long-term Value 1-year data foundation for AI research.
Reusable for future projects.

title: Event 3
content:
Summary Report: “Enterprise AI Agent Architecture, Memory & Security on AWS” (FCAJ AgentCore Deep-Dive) 📌 Event Overview Event Title: FCAJ Deep-Dive Workshop: Enterprise AI Agent Architecture, Memory & Security on AWS. Date & Time: 09:00 – 12:00, November 14, 2026. Location: AWS Vietnam Office, 26th Floor, Bitexco Financial Tower, 02 Hai Trieu Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City. Organizers: First Cloud Journey (FCJ) in collaboration with AWS Community Builders. Attendees: Cloud Solutions Architects, Enterprise Tech Leads, AWS Mentors, and Cloud & AI Intern Builders of the First Cloud AI Journey program. Role: Attendee & Cloud Intern Builder. Event Community Post: Facebook AWS Study Group 🎯 Objectives & Strategic Context As Artificial Intelligence evolves from basic Large Language Models (LLMs) into Autonomous AI Agents, engineering teams confront severe production challenges: how to deploy agents at enterprise scale while maintaining high availability, bulletproof security, persistent multi-tier memory, and strict access governance.
This deep-dive technical workshop focused on bridging this production gap across four key agenda pillars:
The Gap: Disconnect between localized prototyping and production-grade resilient deployment. The Four Pillars: Essential criteria for sustainable operations (Security, Scalability, Reliability, and Cost Optimization). The AWS Answer: AWS reference architecture leveraging AgentCore (Memory & Gateway). The Road Ahead: Production standards and career roadmaps for modern cloud engineers. 🎤 Key Technical Takeaways 1. The Role of Cloud in Enterprise AI The opening session dissected the fundamental operational contrast between running ad-hoc AI workloads and orchestrating on AWS Cloud:
Shared Responsibility Model: AWS manages core physical and compute infrastructure across Multi-AZ regions, freeing engineering teams to focus exclusively on business domain logic, proprietary data, and agent workflows. Four Foundational Value Drivers: Security: Pre-configured regulatory compliance (SOC, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS) and zero-trust perimeter isolation. Scalability: Dynamic auto-scaling to absorb abrupt agent invocation spikes during peak business operations. Reliability: High-availability architectures deployed across multiple Availability Zones with seamless failover. Cost Efficiency: Consumption-based pricing (Pay-as-you-go) eliminating heavy upfront capital expenditure on dedicated compute hardware. 2. The Four Pillars: KMS, IAM & Bedrock Guardrails Securing agentic systems demands a defense-in-depth model combining foundational cloud access control with generative AI risk mitigations:
AWS KMS (Data Privacy): Enforces envelope encryption for data at rest and in transit. Protects proprietary business workflows, recipes, and sensitive customer information. AWS IAM (Access Control): Adheres strictly to the Principle of Least Privilege: “Who enters the storeroom, and who is authorized to cook”. Each agent process receives only the granular permissions strictly required for its task. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (AI-specific Risk): Proactively blocks prompt injections, jailbreaks, and social engineering attempts aimed at tricking agents into unauthorized actions or data disclosures. 3. Production AI Agent Architecture on AWS The workshop unveiled a complete end-to-end production architecture containerized and hosted natively on AWS services:
Continuous Deployment Workflow: Developers build and push versioned agent container images to private Amazon ECR repositories. Network & Compute Isolation: Agent runtimes (Strands Agents) execute on Amazon ECS Fargate inside private subnets across multiple Availability Zones. Egress traffic routes through high-availability NAT Gateways, while inbound traffic enters through an Application Load Balancer (ALB) residing in public subnets. Core Service Integrations: Foundation model invocations route via Amazon Bedrock APIs. Real-time conversation state and ephemeral sessions persist with single-digit millisecond latency on Amazon DynamoDB. Structured telemetry, traces, and metrics stream into Amazon CloudWatch. Sensitive credentials and keys remain safeguarded within AWS Secrets Manager and AWS KMS. 4. Contextual Persistence with AgentCore Memory Overcoming the standard statelessness of LLM interactions requires tiered contextual memory:
Short-term Memory: Manages active chat message threads and ephemeral session states for coherent multi-turn reasoning within a single session. Long-term Memory: Semantic Memory: Vector embeddings of technical documentation and domain facts for targeted RAG retrieval. User Preferences: Preserves personalized user styles, historical selections, and recurring workflows. Summarization Memory: Asynchronously condenses prior interactions to hydrate context windows without exceeding token limits. Episodic Memory: Stores structured action histories and successful resolution paths for future reference. Automatic Memory Extraction Module: Runs asynchronously in the background, harvesting key facts from conversations without adding latency to real-time response generation. Batch API Hydration: Pre-populates agent memory directly from enterprise transactional databases upon session initiation. 5. Two-Door Security Model: Inbound vs Outbound Auth & AgentCore Gateway The session’s standout security architectural principle established: “Two different doors. Two different locks”:
Inbound Auth (User Invoking Agent): Authentication (AuthN): Verifies user identity via JWT tokens issued by Amazon Cognito or enterprise IdPs. Authorization (AuthZ): Evaluates whether the authenticated user has permission to trigger this specific agent. Outbound Auth (Agent Accessing Tools & Upstream Systems on User’s Behalf): Authentication (AuthN): Validates that the agent is legitimately registered and uncompromised. Authorization (AuthZ): Determines whether the agent is authorized to interact with internal databases or APIs strictly on behalf of the user. Workload Access Token (WAT) Mechanism: Agents never hold static database credentials or administrative API keys. Instead, the agent receives a scoped Workload Access Token (WAT) binding both agent and user identities. When invoking downstream tools, the agent passes the WAT to the Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, which validates it against the AgentCore Identity Token Vault and issues short-lived, least-privilege tokens for target API endpoints. 💡 Engineering Takeaways & Capstone Project Alignment Enterprise Architectural Mindset: AI agents in production cannot simply be raw scripts making LLM API calls. They require containerized compute isolation (ECS Fargate in private subnets), load balancing, comprehensive telemetry, and defense-in-depth security. Preventing Privilege Escalation: Decoupling Inbound and Outbound authentication guarantees that agents cannot be coerced into exceeding the operational permissions granted to the requesting user. Capstone Proposal Application: Implementing tiered short-term and long-term memory patterns enables building intelligent, context-aware assistants while actively optimizing token consumption on AWS. 📸 Verification Photo & Event Check-in Figure 1: Author and fellow First Cloud Journey intern builders at the AWS Vietnam Office, 26th Floor, Bitexco Financial Tower.

content:
Week 3 Objectives: Explore Application Modernization paradigms on AWS according to the Application Modernization & Containers curriculum. Investigate enterprise container orchestration ecosystems spanning Amazon ECS Fargate, Amazon EKS, and Red Hat OpenShift on AWS (ROSA).
